items.title: Milky Way simulation reaches record resolution with the help of three supercomputers
items.rationale: Freshest item (11-22): an AI surrogate predicts supernova gas evolution so a star-by-star Milky Way simulation spanning three supercomputers can take longer time steps and run ~20x faster.
items.excerpt: University of Tokyo/RIKEN (Keiya Hirashima) simulated the Milky Way star by star across three supercomputers, using an AI model to predict supernova gas evolution so the galaxy simulation takes longer time steps and runs ~20x faster (SC 2026).

items.title: Putting Google's AI hurricane model to the test
items.rationale: Independent evaluation, not a vendor claim: across 385 tropical cyclones Google's WeatherNext Cyclone beat NOAA's model on 1-5 day intensity and matched human forecasters, but underestimated strength and gave too-narrow uncertainty.
items.excerpt: UAlbany study of 385 tropical cyclones (Geophysical Research Letters) finds Google's WeatherNext Cyclone beat NOAA's hurricane model on intensity at 1-5 days and matched human forecasters, but underestimated strength and gave too-narrow uncertainty ranges.

items.title: AI guardrails falter as tampering drives repeated harassment in simulated conversations
items.rationale: Behavioral-science result with hard numbers: toxic memory, planning prompts or fine-tuning pushed multi-turn harassment rates in Gemini, Llama, Qwen and DeepSeek agents as high as 97%, escalating over turns (ICWSM).
items.excerpt: Georgia State, Georgia Tech and UC Berkeley tested Gemini, Llama, Qwen and DeepSeek agents in multi-turn simulated chats; toxic memory, planning prompts or fine-tuning pushed harassment rates as high as 97% and hostility escalated over turns (ICWSM).

items.title: Collisionality scaling of the tokamak density limit
items.rationale: Fusion physics primary source: ML-guided analysis of a five-machine tokamak database (C-Mod, ASDEX Upgrade, DIII-D, JET, TCV) finds a common edge-collisionality threshold for density-limit disruptions with far fewer false positives than the Greenwald limit.
items.excerpt: MIT PSFC-led team (Maris, Rea et al.) used machine-learning-guided analysis of a multi-machine database (C-Mod, ASDEX Upgrade, DIII-D, JET, TCV) to find a common edge-collisionality threshold for density-limit disruptions with far fewer false positives than the Greenwald limit.

items.title: People prefer AI to human advice in multi-turn conversations but neither changes incentivised behaviour
items.rationale: Controlled behavioral experiment with a sharp split between attitude and action: participants rated an LLM advisor more rational, trustworthy, convincing (and sycophantic) than a human advisor, yet incentivised donation decisions did not change.
items.excerpt: Maier, Lieder, Cheung et al. ran a donation-decision experiment where participants chatted with an LLM advisor, a human, or no one: LLM advisors were judged more rational, trustworthy, convincing and sycophantic, yet donations did not differ across conditions.
